    /// HTTP/2 then HTTP/1.1, as every client of the captures offers them over TCP.
    const H2_HTTP1: &[u8] = b"\x02h2\x08http/1.1";

    #[test]
    fn the_signature_algorithms_go_by_boringssls_names() {
        assert_eq!(
            sigalg_ids(
                "mldsa44:mldsa65:mldsa87:ed25519:ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256:rsa_pss_rsae_sha256:\
                 rsa_pkcs1_sha1:ecdsa_sha1:ecdsa_secp521r1_sha512"
            )
            .expect("names BoringSSL has"),
            [0x0904, 0x0905, 0x0906, 0x0807, 0x0403, 0x0804, 0x0201, 0x0203, 0x0603]
        );
        // ECDSA's names go with their curve; MD5-SHA1 only signs TLS 1.1 and older.
        for refused in [
            "ecdsa_sha256",
            "rsa_pkcs1_md5_sha1",
            "ed448",
            "",
            "RSA+SHA256",
        ] {
            assert!(sigalg_ids(refused).is_err(), "{refused}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn trust_anchor_ids_go_on_the_wire_in_base_128() {
        assert_eq!(
            trust_anchor_ids("11129.9.1").expect("an ID"),
            [4, 0xd6, 0x79, 0x09, 0x01]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            trust_anchor_ids("44947.2.6:0").expect("two IDs"),
            [5, 0x82, 0xdf, 0x13, 0x02, 0x06, 1, 0x00]
        );
        // Chrome's, as its ClientHello carries them: 184 bytes.
        let chrome = trust_anchor_ids(CHROME_TRUST_ANCHORS).expect("Chrome's");
        assert_eq!(chrome.len(), 184);
        assert_eq!(chrome[..6], [5, 0x82, 0xdf, 0x13, 0x02, 0x01]);
        let too_long = ["18446744073709551615"; 30].join(".");
        for refused in [
            "",
            "1..2",
            ".1",
            "1.",
            "01",
            "1.x",
            "1:",
            "18446744073709551616",
            too_long.as_str(),
        ] {
            assert!(trust_anchor_ids(refused).is_err(), "{refused}");
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn the_client_hello_carries_the_extensions_of_the_options() {
        // Chrome's of October 2026, from its ClientHello: GREASE then ML-DSA first among the
        // signature algorithms, brotli, ALPS for HTTP/2 under the new codepoint, ECH GREASE,
        // its trust anchors and 6000 bytes of padding asked of the server.
        let chrome = Fingerprint {
            groups: "X25519MLKEM768:X25519:P-256:P-384".to_string(),
            grease_sigalgs: true,
            sigalgs: Some(CHROME_SIGALGS.to_string()),
            cert_compression: Some("brotli".to_string()),
            alps: Some("new".to_string()),
            trust_anchors: Some(CHROME_TRUST_ANCHORS.to_string()),
            server_padding: Some("6000".to_string()),
            ech_grease: true,
            ..Fingerprint::default()
        };
        let hello = hello_offering(&chrome, H2_HTTP1).await;
        assert!(hello.has_grease_signature_algorithm());
        assert_eq!(
            hello.signature_algorithms()[1..],
            [
                0x0904, 0x0905, 0x0906, 0x0403, 0x0804, 0x0401, 0x0503, 0x0805, 0x0501, 0x0806,
                0x0601
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(hello.cert_compression(), [2]);
        // ALPS for HTTP/2 alone, not for HTTP/1.1, under the new codepoint alone.
        assert_eq!(hello.alps(0x44cd), Some(vec![b"h2".to_vec()]));
        assert_eq!(hello.alps(0x4469), None);
        assert!(hello.offers_ech());
        let anchors = trust_anchor_ids(CHROME_TRUST_ANCHORS).expect("Chrome's");
        let mut wire = (anchors.len() as u16).to_be_bytes().to_vec();
        wire.extend(&anchors);
        assert_eq!(hello.extension(0xca34), Some(wire.as_slice()));
        assert_eq!(hello.server_padding(), Some(6000));
        // OCSP, signed certificate timestamps and the session ticket, as Chrome's.
        assert!(hello.has_extension(5) && hello.has_extension(18) && hello.has_extension(35));

        // Chrome 120's: ALPS under the old codepoint, its eight signature algorithms without
        // GREASE or ML-DSA, and neither trust anchors nor server padding.
        let chrome_120 = Fingerprint {
            groups: "X25519:P-256:P-384".to_string(),
            sigalgs: Some(CHROME_120_SIGALGS.to_string()),
            cert_compression: Some("brotli".to_string()),
            alps: Some("old".to_string()),
            ech_grease: true,
            ..Fingerprint::default()
        };
        let hello = hello_offering(&chrome_120, H2_HTTP1).await;
        assert_eq!(
            hello.signature_algorithms(),
            [0x0403, 0x0804, 0x0401, 0x0503, 0x0805, 0x0501, 0x0806, 0x0601]
        );
        assert_eq!(hello.alps(0x4469), Some(vec![b"h2".to_vec()]));
        assert_eq!(hello.alps(0x44cd), None);
        assert_eq!(hello.cert_compression(), [2]);
        assert!(hello.offers_ech());
        assert!(!hello.has_extension(0xca34));
        assert_eq!(hello.server_padding(), None);

        // Firefox's: zlib, brotli and zstd, no session ticket, and the extensions in one order,
        // BoringSSL's, the same on every handshake.
        let firefox = Fingerprint {
            grease: false,
            sigalgs: Some(FIREFOX_SIGALGS.to_string()),
            cert_compression: Some("zlib:brotli:zstd".to_string()),
            ech_grease: true,
            session_ticket: false,
            permute_extensions: false,
            ..Fingerprint::default()
        };
        let first = hello_offering(&firefox, H2_HTTP1).await;
        assert_eq!(
            first.signature_algorithms(),
            [
                0x0403, 0x0503, 0x0603, 0x0804, 0x0805, 0x0806, 0x0401, 0x0501, 0x0601, 0x0203,
                0x0201
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(first.cert_compression(), [1, 2, 3]);
        assert!(!first.has_extension(35));
        assert!(first.offers_ech());
        assert!(first.has_extension(5) && first.has_extension(18));
        assert_eq!(first.alps(0x44cd), None);
        assert_eq!(first.alps(0x4469), None);
        for _ in 0..3 {
            let again = hello_offering(&firefox, H2_HTTP1).await;
            assert_eq!(again.extension_types(), first.extension_types());
        }
        assert_eq!(
            first.extension_types(),
            [0, 0xfe0d, 23, 0xff01, 10, 11, 16, 5, 13, 18, 51, 45, 43, 27]
        );

        // Python's: no OCSP, no signed certificate timestamps, one order, and so no padding
        // extension, which BoringSSL adds when a shuffled order ends on an empty extension.
        let python = Fingerprint {
            grease: false,
            ocsp_stapling: false,
            sct: false,
            permute_extensions: false,
            ..Fingerprint::default()
        };
        for _ in 0..3 {
            let hello = hello_offering(&python, H2_HTTP1).await;
            assert_eq!(
                hello.extension_types(),
                [0, 23, 0xff01, 10, 11, 35, 16, 13, 51, 45, 43]
            );
        }
    }

    extern "C" {
        fn CBB_add_bytes(cbb: *mut c_void, data: *const u8, len: usize) -> c_int;
        fn SSL_has_application_settings(ssl: *const c_void) -> c_int;
        fn SSL_get0_peer_application_settings(
            ssl: *const c_void,
            out_data: *mut *const u8,
            out_len: *mut usize,
        );
    }

    /// How many certificates the servers of the tests compressed.
    static COMPRESSED: std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize = std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0);

    /// Hands BoringSSL, in `out`, what `compress` makes of the certificate at `input`, as a
    /// server compresses one.
    unsafe fn compressed(
        out: *mut c_void,
        input: *const u8,
        input_len: usize,
        compress: fn(&[u8]) -> Vec<u8>,
    ) -> c_int {
        let input = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(input, input_len) };
        let bytes = compress(input);
        COMPRESSED.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
        unsafe { CBB_add_bytes(out, bytes.as_ptr(), bytes.len()) }
    }

    fn zlib_of(input: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        use std::io::Write;
        let mut encoder =
            flate2::write::ZlibEncoder::new(Vec::new(), flate2::Compression::default());
        encoder.write_all(input).expect("zlib");
        encoder.finish().expect("zlib")
    }

    fn zstd_of(input: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        zstd::bulk::compress(input, 3).expect("zstd")
    }

    /// Zstd whose frame asks for a window of 2^`window_log` bytes, whatever the input: without
    /// its length, which would make the window the input's.
    fn zstd_window_of(input: &[u8], window_log: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
        use std::io::Write;
        let mut encoder = zstd::stream::write::Encoder::new(Vec::new(), 3).expect("zstd");
        encoder.include_contentsize(false).expect("no length");
        encoder.window_log(window_log).expect("the window");
        encoder.write_all(input).expect("zstd");
        encoder.finish().expect("zstd")
    }

    /// Brotli (RFC 7932) without compression, which the brotli crate the core decompresses with
    /// cannot make: a window of 2^16, the input in meta-blocks stored as they are, 65536 bytes
    /// at most each, then an empty last one.
    fn brotli_of(input: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        struct Bits {
            out: Vec<u8>,
            byte: u8,
            used: u32,
        }
        impl Bits {
            /// The `count` low bits of `value`, the lowest first.
            fn put(&mut self, value: u32, count: u32) {
                for bit in 0..count {
                    self.byte |= (((value >> bit) & 1) as u8) << self.used;
                    self.used += 1;
                    if self.used == 8 {
                        self.align();
                    }
                }
            }
            fn align(&mut self) {
                if self.used > 0 {
                    self.out.push(self.byte);
                    self.byte = 0;
                    self.used = 0;
                }
            }
        }
        let mut bits = Bits {
            out: Vec::new(),
            byte: 0,
            used: 0,
        };
        bits.put(0, 1); // WBITS: 16
        for block in input.chunks(65536) {
            bits.put(0, 1); // ISLAST
            bits.put(0, 2); // MNIBBLES: 4
            bits.put(block.len() as u32 - 1, 16); // MLEN - 1
            bits.put(1, 1); // ISUNCOMPRESSED
            bits.align();
            bits.out.extend_from_slice(block);
        }
        bits.put(1, 1); // ISLAST
        bits.put(1, 1); // ISLASTEMPTY
        bits.align();
        bits.out
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_test_brotli_is_brotli() {
        let input: Vec<u8> = (0..70000u32).map(|n| (n % 251) as u8).collect();
        let mut out = vec![0u8; input.len()];
        assert!(brotli_into(&brotli_of(&input), &mut out));
        assert_eq!(out, input);
    }

    /// Whether a handshake of `client`, offering HTTP/2, goes through with a server on this
    /// machine that compresses its certificate as algorithm `id` with `compress`.
    async fn handshake_with_compression(
        client: &Fingerprint,
        id: u16,
        compress: CertCompressFn,
    ) -> bool {
        let pair = crate::account::generate_masque_keypair().expect("a key and a certificate");
        let mut builder =
            boring::ssl::SslAcceptor::mozilla_intermediate_v5(SslMethod::tls()).expect("tls");
        builder
            .set_certificate(&X509::from_pem(&pair.cert_pem).expect("a certificate"))
            .expect("the certificate");
        builder
            .set_private_key(&PKey::private_key_from_pem(&pair.key_pem).expect("a key"))
            .expect("the key");
        let added = unsafe {
            SSL_CTX_add_cert_compression_alg(builder.as_ptr().cast(), id, Some(compress), None)
        };
        assert_eq!(added, 1, "the server's compression");
        let acceptor = builder.build();
        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0")
            .await
            .expect("a port");
        let address = listener.local_addr().expect("its address");
        let server = tokio::spawn(async move {
            let (tcp, _) = listener.accept().await.expect("a connection");
            if let Ok(mut stream) = tokio_boring::accept(&acceptor, tcp).await {
                // Until the client hangs up.
                let mut byte = [0u8; 1];
                let _ = tokio::io::AsyncReadExt::read(&mut stream, &mut byte).await;
            }
        });
        let mut connector = boring::ssl::SslConnector::builder(SslMethod::tls()).expect("tls");
        client
            .apply(&mut connector, b"\x02h2")
            .expect("the fingerprint");
        let mut config = connector.build().configure().expect("a configuration");
        client
            .prepare(&mut config, b"\x02h2")
            .expect("what goes on the connection");
        let tcp = tokio::net::TcpStream::connect(address)
            .await
            .expect("a connection");
        let done = tokio_boring::connect(config, "localhost", tcp)
            .await
            .is_ok();
        server.await.expect("the server");
        done
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_certificate_sent_compressed_is_decompressed() {
        unsafe extern "C" fn zlib_server(
            _: *mut c_void,
            out: *mut c_void,
            input: *const u8,
            len: usize,
        ) -> c_int {
            unsafe { compressed(out, input, len, zlib_of) }
        }
        unsafe extern "C" fn brotli_server(
            _: *mut c_void,
            out: *mut c_void,
            input: *const u8,
            len: usize,
        ) -> c_int {
            unsafe { compressed(out, input, len, brotli_of) }
        }
        unsafe extern "C" fn zstd_server(
            _: *mut c_void,
            out: *mut c_void,
            input: *const u8,
            len: usize,
        ) -> c_int {
            unsafe { compressed(out, input, len, zstd_of) }
        }
        // A certificate one byte short of the length the server gives, and one byte over it.
        unsafe extern "C" fn short_zlib_server(
            _: *mut c_void,
            out: *mut c_void,
            input: *const u8,
            len: usize,
        ) -> c_int {
            unsafe { compressed(out, input, len, |input| zlib_of(&input[..input.len() - 1])) }
        }
        unsafe extern "C" fn long_brotli_server(
            _: *mut c_void,
            out: *mut c_void,
            input: *const u8,
            len: usize,
        ) -> c_int {
            unsafe { compressed(out, input, len, |input| brotli_of(&[input, &[0]].concat())) }
        }
        unsafe extern "C" fn short_brotli_server(
            _: *mut c_void,
            out: *mut c_void,
            input: *const u8,
            len: usize,
        ) -> c_int {
            unsafe {
                compressed(out, input, len, |input| {
                    brotli_of(&input[..input.len() - 1])
                })
            }
        }
        unsafe extern "C" fn long_zstd_server(
            _: *mut c_void,
            out: *mut c_void,
            input: *const u8,
            len: usize,
        ) -> c_int {
            unsafe { compressed(out, input, len, |input| zstd_of(&[input, &[0]].concat())) }
        }
        // A frame that asks for the largest window the core takes, and one that asks for twice.
        unsafe extern "C" fn widest_zstd_server(
            _: *mut c_void,
            out: *mut c_void,
            input: *const u8,
            len: usize,
        ) -> c_int {
            unsafe {
                compressed(out, input, len, |input| {
                    zstd_window_of(input, ZSTD_WINDOW_LOG_MAX)
                })
            }
        }
        unsafe extern "C" fn too_wide_zstd_server(
            _: *mut c_void,
            out: *mut c_void,
            input: *const u8,
            len: usize,
        ) -> c_int {
            unsafe {
                compressed(out, input, len, |input| {
                    zstd_window_of(input, ZSTD_WINDOW_LOG_MAX + 1)
                })
            }
        }
        let offering = |list: &str| Fingerprint {
            cert_compression: Some(list.to_string()),
            ..Fingerprint::default()
        };
        let count = || COMPRESSED.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);

        for (name, id, server) in [
            ("zlib", 1, zlib_server as CertCompressFn),
            ("brotli", 2, brotli_server),
            ("zstd", 3, zstd_server),
        ] {
            let before = count();
            assert!(
                handshake_with_compression(&offering(name), id, server).await,
                "{name}"
            );
            assert_eq!(
                count(),
                before + 1,
                "{name}: the certificate went compressed"
            );
            // Offered among the others.
            assert!(
                handshake_with_compression(&offering("zlib:brotli:zstd"), id, server).await,
                "{name} among the three"
            );
        }
        // The decompressed certificate is exactly as long as the server said, or the
        // handshake fails.
        for (name, id, server) in [
            ("zlib", 1, short_zlib_server as CertCompressFn),
            ("brotli", 2, short_brotli_server),
            ("brotli", 2, long_brotli_server),
            ("zstd", 3, long_zstd_server),
        ] {
            let before = count();
            assert!(
                !handshake_with_compression(&offering(name), id, server).await,
                "{name}"
            );
            assert_eq!(count(), before + 1, "{name}: the server compressed");
        }
        // A zstd frame may ask for a window of 8 MiB at most: a server gets no more of the
        // client's memory than that.
        let zstd = offering("zstd");
        assert!(handshake_with_compression(&zstd, 3, widest_zstd_server).await);
        assert!(!handshake_with_compression(&zstd, 3, too_wide_zstd_server).await);
        // Without the option, the certificate goes as it is.
        let before = count();
        assert!(handshake_with_compression(&Fingerprint::default(), 2, brotli_server).await);
        assert_eq!(count(), before);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn alps_goes_through_with_a_server_that_takes_it() {
        for (codepoint, new) in [("new", true), ("old", false)] {
            let pair = crate::account::generate_masque_keypair().expect("a key and a certificate");
            let mut builder =
                boring::ssl::SslAcceptor::mozilla_intermediate_v5(SslMethod::tls()).expect("tls");
            builder
                .set_certificate(&X509::from_pem(&pair.cert_pem).expect("a certificate"))
                .expect("the certificate");
            builder
                .set_private_key(&PKey::private_key_from_pem(&pair.key_pem).expect("a key"))
                .expect("the key");
            builder.set_alpn_select_callback(|_, offered| {
                boring::ssl::select_next_proto(b"\x02h2", offered)
                    .ok_or(boring::ssl::AlpnError::NOACK)
            });
            let acceptor = builder.build();
            let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0")
                .await
                .expect("a port");
            let address = listener.local_addr().expect("its address");
            let server = tokio::spawn(async move {
                let (tcp, _) = listener.accept().await.expect("a connection");
                let ssl = Ssl::new(acceptor.context()).expect("a connection");
                unsafe {
                    SSL_set_alps_use_new_codepoint(ssl.as_ptr().cast(), c_int::from(new));
                    let settings = b"the server's settings";
                    let added = SSL_add_application_settings(
                        ssl.as_ptr().cast(),
                        b"h2".as_ptr(),
                        2,
                        settings.as_ptr(),
                        settings.len(),
                    );
                    assert_eq!(added, 1);
                }
                if let Ok(mut stream) = tokio_boring::SslStreamBuilder::new(ssl, tcp).accept().await
                {
                    let mut byte = [0u8; 1];
                    let _ = tokio::io::AsyncReadExt::read(&mut stream, &mut byte).await;
                }
            });
            let client = Fingerprint {
                alps: Some(codepoint.to_string()),
                ..Fingerprint::default()
            };
            let mut connector = boring::ssl::SslConnector::builder(SslMethod::tls()).expect("tls");
            client
                .apply(&mut connector, H2_HTTP1)
                .expect("the fingerprint");
            let mut config = connector.build().configure().expect("a configuration");
            client
                .prepare(&mut config, H2_HTTP1)
                .expect("what goes on the connection");
            let tcp = tokio::net::TcpStream::connect(address)
                .await
                .expect("a connection");
            let stream = tokio_boring::connect(config, "localhost", tcp)
                .await
                .expect("a handshake");
            let ssl = stream.ssl();
            assert_eq!(
                ssl.selected_alpn_protocol(),
                Some(&b"h2"[..]),
                "{codepoint}"
            );
            assert_eq!(
                unsafe { SSL_has_application_settings(ssl.as_ptr().cast()) },
                1,
                "{codepoint}"
            );
            let (mut data, mut len) = (ptr::null(), 0);
            unsafe { SSL_get0_peer_application_settings(ssl.as_ptr().cast(), &mut data, &mut len) };
            assert_eq!(
                unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(data, len) },
                b"the server's settings",
                "{codepoint}"
            );
            drop(stream);
            server.await.expect("the server");
        }
    }

    /// An ECHConfig: `version`, config id 7, the KEM `kem` with a key of `key_len` bytes, the
    /// cipher suites `suites` as (KDF, AEAD), the public name `name`, and `extensions` as they
    /// go on the wire.
    fn config(
        version: u16,
        kem: u16,
        key_len: usize,
        suites: &[(u16, u16)],
        name: &str,
        extensions: &[u8],
    ) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut contents = vec![7];
        contents.extend_from_slice(&kem.to_be_bytes());
        contents.extend_from_slice(&(key_len as u16).to_be_bytes());
        contents.extend(std::iter::repeat_n(0x42, key_len));
        contents.extend_from_slice(&((suites.len() * 4) as u16).to_be_bytes());
        for (kdf, aead) in suites {
            contents.extend_from_slice(&kdf.to_be_bytes());
            contents.extend_from_slice(&aead.to_be_bytes());
        }
        contents.push(0);
        contents.push(name.len() as u8);
        contents.extend_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        contents.extend_from_slice(&(extensions.len() as u16).to_be_bytes());
        contents.extend_from_slice(extensions);
        let mut config = version.to_be_bytes().to_vec();
        config.extend_from_slice(&(contents.len() as u16).to_be_bytes());
        config.extend(contents);
        config
    }

    fn list(configs: &[Vec<u8>]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let body = configs.concat();
        let mut list = (body.len() as u16).to_be_bytes().to_vec();
        list.extend(body);
        list
    }

    /// A config like Cloudflare's: X25519, HKDF-SHA256 with AES-128-GCM.
    fn offered(name: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
        config(0xfe0d, 0x0020, 32, &[(1, 1)], name, &[])
    }

    #[test]
    fn cloudflares_key_is_one_boringssl_offers() {
        // Cloudflare's key of cloudflare-ech.com on 2026-10-01.
        let key = decode_ech_config_list(
            "AEX+DQBBrwAgACCbK1mYDYFz/BAn6S5t+Q/v+Oej3eFNxtPWgz50fNnFPAAEAAEAAQASY2xvdWRmbGFyZS1lY2guY29tAAA=",
        )
        .expect("base64");
        assert_eq!(check_ech_config_list(&key), Ok(()));
        // The same fields as built here, the key aside.
        let mut built = list(&[offered("cloudflare-ech.com")]);
        built[2 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 2..][..32].copy_from_slice(&key[11..43]);
        built[6] = key[6];
        assert_eq!(built, key);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_key_boringssl_would_pass_over_is_turned_down() {
        // Each parses, so BoringSSL would take it, offer nothing, and send the name in the clear.
        let passed_over = [
            config(0xfe0c, 0x0020, 32, &[(1, 1)], "cloudflare-ech.com", &[]),
            // P-256, its key as long as an X25519 one so that only the KEM tells them apart.
            config(0xfe0d, 0x0010, 32, &[(1, 1)], "cloudflare-ech.com", &[]),
            config(0xfe0d, 0x0020, 32, &[(2, 1)], "cloudflare-ech.com", &[]),
            config(0xfe0d, 0x0020, 32, &[(1, 4)], "cloudflare-ech.com", &[]),
            config(
                0xfe0d,
                0x0020,
                32,
                &[(1, 1)],
                "cloudflare-ech.com",
                &[0x80, 1, 0, 0],
            ),
            offered("192.0.2.1"),
            offered("example.0x1F"),
            offered("-example.com"),
            offered("example-.com"),
            offered("example..com"),
            offered("example.com."),
            offered("exa_mple.com"),
            offered(&"a".repeat(64)),
        ];
        for config in passed_over {
            let list = list(&[config]);
            assert!(check_ech_config_list(&list).is_err(), "{list:02x?}");
            assert!(usable_retry(&list).is_none());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_first_config_boringssl_can_offer_is_the_one_it_offers() {
        let older = config(0xfe0c, 0x0020, 32, &[(1, 1)], "x.example", &[]);
        assert_eq!(
            check_ech_config_list(&list(&[older, offered("a.example")])),
            Ok(())
        );
        // An extension that is not mandatory is passed over, and one good suite is enough.
        let optional = config(
            0xfe0d,
            0x0020,
            32,
            &[(2, 1), (1, 3)],
            "a.example",
            &[0, 1, 0, 1, 9],
        );
        assert_eq!(check_ech_config_list(&list(&[optional])), Ok(()));
        // Only a last label that is a number disqualifies a name.
        assert_eq!(
            check_ech_config_list(&list(&[offered("0x1f.example")])),
            Ok(())
        );
        assert_eq!(check_ech_config_list(&list(&[offered("a.0x1g")])), Ok(()));
        assert_eq!(check_ech_config_list(&list(&[offered("a.b1")])), Ok(()));
        // A config it picks with a key of the wrong length fails the handshake: no later one counts.
        let short = config(0xfe0d, 0x0020, 31, &[(1, 1)], "a.example", &[]);
        assert!(check_ech_config_list(&list(&[short, offered("a.example")])).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_list_boringssl_cannot_parse_is_turned_down() {
        let mut trailing = list(&[offered("a.example")]);
        trailing.push(0);
        let mut cut = list(&[offered("a.example")]);
        cut.pop();
        // A config it would pass over still has to parse: here its extensions are cut short.
        let broken = list(&[
            offered("a.example"),
            config(0xfe0d, 0x0020, 32, &[(1, 1)], "a.example", &[0]),
        ]);
        let no_key = list(&[config(0xfe0d, 0x0020, 0, &[(1, 1)], "a.example", &[])]);
        let no_name = list(&[offered("")]);
        // What BoringSSL hands out for retry configs when it has none.
        let placeholder = vec![0xfe, 0x0d, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff];
        for bad in [
            vec![],
            vec![0, 0],
            trailing,
            cut,
            broken,
            no_key,
            no_name,
            placeholder,
        ] {
            assert!(check_ech_config_list(&bad).is_err(), "{bad:02x?}");
            assert!(ensure_offerable(&bad).is_err());
        }
    }

    /// Whether BoringSSL offers ECH from `list` in the ClientHello it sends to a server on this
    /// machine: None when it takes no such list, or sends no ClientHello at all.
    async fn boringssl_offers(list: &[u8]) -> Option<bool> {
        let mut builder = boring::ssl::SslConnector::builder(SslMethod::tls()).expect("tls");
        Fingerprint::default()
            .apply(&mut builder, b"\x02h2")
            .expect("the fingerprint");
        let mut config = builder.build().configure().expect("a configuration");
        config.set_ech_config_list(list).ok()?;
        let (server, hello) = client_hello::catch().await;
        let tcp = tokio::net::TcpStream::connect(server)
            .await
            .expect("a connection");
        let _ = tokio_boring::connect(config, "a.example", tcp).await;
        hello.await.ok().map(|hello| hello.offers_ech())
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn the_key_check_says_what_boringssl_does() {
        // The fingerprint sends no GREASE ECH, so an ECH extension in the ClientHello means
        // BoringSSL took a config from the list.
        let older = config(0xfe0c, 0x0020, 32, &[(1, 1)], "x.example", &[]);
        let short = config(0xfe0d, 0x0020, 31, &[(1, 1)], "a.example", &[]);
        let lists = [
            decode_ech_config_list(CLOUDFLARE_ECH).expect("base64"),
            list(&[older.clone(), offered("a.example")]),
            list(&[config(
                0xfe0d,
                0x0020,
                32,
                &[(2, 1), (1, 3)],
                "a.example",
                &[0, 1, 0, 1, 9],
            )]),
            list(&[offered("0x1f.example")]),
            list(&[older]),
            list(&[config(0xfe0d, 0x0010, 32, &[(1, 1)], "a.example", &[])]),
            list(&[config(0xfe0d, 0x0020, 32, &[(2, 1)], "a.example", &[])]),
            list(&[config(0xfe0d, 0x0020, 32, &[(1, 4)], "a.example", &[])]),
            list(&[config(
                0xfe0d,
                0x0020,
                32,
                &[(1, 1)],
                "a.example",
                &[0x80, 1, 0, 0],
            )]),
            list(&[offered("192.0.2.1")]),
            list(&[offered("example.0x1F")]),
            list(&[offered("example.com.")]),
            list(&[offered("exa_mple.com")]),
            list(&[short, offered("a.example")]),
            list(&[config(0xfe0d, 0x0020, 0, &[(1, 1)], "a.example", &[])]),
            vec![0xfe, 0x0d, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff],
        ];
        for list in lists {
            let sent = boringssl_offers(&list).await;
            assert_eq!(
                check_ech_config_list(&list).is_ok(),
                sent == Some(true),
                "{list:02x?}: BoringSSL {sent:?}"
            );
        }
    }
}

/// A ClientHello as a server reads it, and a server on this machine that reads one and hangs
/// up, for the tests of the handshakes that list cipher suites.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod client_hello {
    use tokio::io::AsyncReadExt;

    pub struct ClientHello {
        /// The cipher suites, in order.
        pub suites: Vec<u16>,
        /// The extensions, in order: their type and what they carry.
        pub extensions: Vec<(u16, Vec<u8>)>,
    }

    /// Whether `value` is a GREASE value (RFC 8701).
    fn grease(value: u16) -> bool {
        value & 0x0f0f == 0x0a0a && value >> 8 == value & 0xff
    }

    fn be16(bytes: &[u8], at: usize) -> usize {
        u16::from_be_bytes([bytes[at], bytes[at + 1]]) as usize
    }

    impl ClientHello {
        /// What the extension `kind` carries, when it is there.
        pub fn extension(&self, kind: u16) -> Option<&[u8]> {
            self.extensions
                .iter()
                .find(|(k, _)| *k == kind)
                .map(|(_, data)| data.as_slice())
        }

        /// The algorithms of compress_certificate, in order; empty without it.
        pub fn cert_compression(&self) -> Vec<u16> {
            self.extension(27)
                .map(|data| {
                    data[1..1 + data[0] as usize]
                        .chunks(2)
                        .map(|pair| u16::from_be_bytes([pair[0], pair[1]]))
                        .collect()
                })
                .unwrap_or_default()
        }

        /// The protocols of application_settings, under the codepoint `kind` (0x44cd or 0x4469),
        /// in order, when it is there.
        pub fn alps(&self, kind: u16) -> Option<Vec<Vec<u8>>> {
            let data = self.extension(kind)?;
            let mut protocols = Vec::new();
            let mut at = 2;
            while at < data.len() {
                let len = data[at] as usize;
                protocols.push(data[at + 1..at + 1 + len].to_vec());
                at += 1 + len;
            }
            Some(protocols)
        }

        /// The bytes of padding the server_padding extension (0x12e0) asks for, when it is there.
        pub fn server_padding(&self) -> Option<u16> {
            self.extension(0x12e0)
                .map(|data| u16::from_be_bytes([data[0], data[1]]))
        }

        /// The TLS 1.2 cipher suites: GREASE and the TLS 1.3 ones left out.
        pub fn tls12_suites(&self) -> Vec<u16> {
            self.suites
                .iter()
                .copied()
                .filter(|suite| !grease(*suite) && !(0x1301..=0x1305).contains(suite))
                .collect()
        }

        /// The versions of supported_versions, GREASE left out.
        pub fn versions(&self) -> Vec<u16> {
            let data = self.extension(43).expect("supported_versions");
            data[1..1 + data[0] as usize]
                .chunks(2)
                .map(|pair| u16::from_be_bytes([pair[0], pair[1]]))
                .filter(|version| !grease(*version))
                .collect()
        }

        /// The name in server_name.
        pub fn server_name(&self) -> Option<String> {
            let data = self.extension(0)?;
            Some(String::from_utf8_lossy(&data[5..5 + be16(data, 3)]).into_owned())
        }

        /// Whether it offers ECH: encrypted_client_hello.
        pub fn offers_ech(&self) -> bool {
            self.extension(0xfe0d).is_some()
        }

        /// The protocols of application_layer_protocol_negotiation, in order.
        pub fn alpn(&self) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {
            let data = self.extension(16).expect("ALPN");
            let mut protocols = Vec::new();
            let mut at = 2;
            while at < data.len() {
                let len = data[at] as usize;
                protocols.push(data[at + 1..at + 1 + len].to_vec());
                at += 1 + len;
            }
            protocols
        }

        /// Whether a GREASE value leads its cipher suites.
        pub fn has_grease(&self) -> bool {
            self.suites.first().is_some_and(|suite| grease(*suite))
        }

        /// Whether one of its extensions is a GREASE one.
        pub fn has_grease_extension(&self) -> bool {
            self.extensions.iter().any(|(kind, _)| grease(*kind))
        }

        /// Whether it carries the extension `kind`.
        pub fn has_extension(&self, kind: u16) -> bool {
            self.extension(kind).is_some()
        }

        /// The types of its extensions, in order.
        pub fn extension_types(&self) -> Vec<u16> {
            self.extensions.iter().map(|(kind, _)| *kind).collect()
        }

        /// The groups of supported_groups, in order, GREASE left out.
        pub fn groups(&self) -> Vec<u16> {
            let data = self.extension(10).expect("supported_groups");
            data[2..2 + be16(data, 0)]
                .chunks(2)
                .map(|pair| u16::from_be_bytes([pair[0], pair[1]]))
                .filter(|group| !grease(*group))
                .collect()
        }

        /// The groups of the shares of key_share, in order, GREASE among them.
        fn key_share_groups(&self) -> Vec<u16> {
            let data = self.extension(51).expect("key_share");
            let mut groups = Vec::new();
            let mut at = 2;
            while at + 4 <= data.len() {
                groups.push(be16(data, at) as u16);
                at += 4 + be16(data, at + 2);
            }
            groups
        }

        /// The groups of the shares of key_share, in order, GREASE left out.
        pub fn key_shares(&self) -> Vec<u16> {
            self.key_share_groups()
                .into_iter()
                .filter(|group| !grease(*group))
                .collect()
        }

        /// Whether one of the shares of key_share is a GREASE one.
        pub fn has_grease_key_share(&self) -> bool {
            self.key_share_groups().into_iter().any(grease)
        }

        /// The TLS 1.3 cipher suites, in order.
        pub fn tls13_suites(&self) -> Vec<u16> {
            self.suites
                .iter()
                .copied()
                .filter(|suite| (0x1301..=0x1305).contains(suite))
                .collect()
        }

        /// The signature algorithms of signature_algorithms, in order, GREASE among them.
        pub fn signature_algorithms(&self) -> Vec<u16> {
            let data = self.extension(13).expect("signature_algorithms");
            data[2..2 + be16(data, 0)]
                .chunks(2)
                .map(|pair| u16::from_be_bytes([pair[0], pair[1]]))
                .collect()
        }

        /// Whether a GREASE value leads its signature algorithms.
        pub fn has_grease_signature_algorithm(&self) -> bool {
            self.signature_algorithms()
                .first()
                .is_some_and(|value| grease(*value))
        }
    }

    /// The ClientHello in `record`, a TLS record as it goes over the wire.
    pub fn parse(record: &[u8]) -> ClientHello {
        assert_eq!(record[0], 0x16, "a handshake record");
        let message = &record[5..5 + be16(record, 3)];
        assert_eq!(message[0], 1, "a ClientHello");
        parse_body(&message[4..])
    }

    /// The ClientHello whose body is `hello`: what follows its handshake header, as BoringSSL
    /// hands a server the ClientHello of a QUIC connection.
    pub fn parse_body(hello: &[u8]) -> ClientHello {
        let mut at = 2 + 32;
        at += 1 + hello[at] as usize;
        let suites = hello[at + 2..at + 2 + be16(hello, at)]
            .chunks(2)
            .map(|pair| u16::from_be_bytes([pair[0], pair[1]]))
            .collect();
        at += 2 + be16(hello, at);
        at += 1 + hello[at] as usize;
        let end = at + 2 + be16(hello, at);
        at += 2;
        let mut extensions = Vec::new();
        while at + 4 <= end {
            let len = be16(hello, at + 2);
            extensions.push((be16(hello, at) as u16, hello[at + 4..at + 4 + len].to_vec()));
            at += 4 + len;
        }
        ClientHello { suites, extensions }
    }

    /// Chrome's TLS 1.2 suites, in the order BoringSSL gives Chrome's rule on this machine,
    /// which depends on its AES hardware.
    pub fn chrome_tls12_suites() -> Vec<u16> {
        super::tls12_ciphers(super::CHROME_CIPHERS)
            .expect("Chrome's rule")
            .iter()
            .map(|(id, _)| *id)
            .collect()
    }

    /// Listens on this machine: the task ends with the first ClientHello sent there, read
    /// before the server hangs up, and fails when none comes within ten seconds.
    pub async fn catch() -> (std::net::SocketAddr, tokio::task::JoinHandle<ClientHello>) {
        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0")
            .await
            .expect("a port");
        let address = listener.local_addr().expect("its address");
        let caught = tokio::spawn(async move {
            let (mut tcp, _) =
                tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(10), listener.accept())
                    .await
                    .expect("a connection within ten seconds")
                    .expect("a connection");
            let mut record = vec![0u8; 5];
            tcp.read_exact(&mut record).await.expect("a record header");
            let len = be16(&record, 3);
            record.resize(5 + len, 0);
            tcp.read_exact(&mut record[5..]).await.expect("the record");
            parse(&record)
        });
        (address, caught)
    }
}

use std::net::SocketAddr;
use std::path::PathBuf;

use crate::error::{AetherError, Result};

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum TorError {
    #[error("this build has no tor support; rebuild with `cargo build --release --features tor`")]
    NotBuiltIn,
    #[error("tor cannot dial through {tunnel}: {reason}")]
    Tunnel { tunnel: SocketAddr, reason: String },
    #[error("tor cannot dial through the upstream proxy at {0}: it takes a socks5 address, with a password only on this machine")]
    UpstreamProxy(String),
    #[error("none of the bridges could be read by tor")]
    NoReadableBridges,
    #[error("transport '{protocol}': {reason}")]
    Transport { protocol: String, reason: String },
    #[error("tor configuration: {0}")]
    Configuration(String),
    #[error("tor client: {0}")]
    Client(String),
    #[error("{0}")]
    Bootstrap(String),
    #[error("no headway for {0}s")]
    NoHeadway(u64),
    #[error("tor came up but could not reach {host}:{port}: {reason}")]
    Unreachable {
        host: String,
        port: u16,
        reason: String,
    },
    #[error("tor came up but {host}:{port} stayed silent for {seconds}s")]
    Silent {
        host: String,
        port: u16,
        seconds: u64,
    },
    #[error("no answer in {0}s")]
    NoAnswer(u64),
    #[error("the bridges you gave need a pluggable transport that is not installed; {0}")]
    TransportMissing(&'static str),
    #[error("tor is blocked on this network and no pluggable transport is installed, so no bridge can be used; {0}")]
    BlockedWithoutTransport(&'static str),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Mode {
    Off,
    Chain,
    Reverse,
    Only,
}

impl Mode {
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Mode::Off => "off",
            Mode::Chain => "tor through the tunnel",
            Mode::Reverse => "the tunnel through tor",
            Mode::Only => "tor alone",
        }
    }
}

pub fn mode() -> Mode {
    let raw = match crate::settings::var("AETHER_TOR") {
        Ok(value) => value.trim().to_lowercase(),
        Err(_) => return Mode::Off,
    };

    match raw.as_str() {
        "" | "0" | "off" | "false" | "no" => Mode::Off,
        "reverse" | "rev" | "warp-over-tor" => Mode::Reverse,
        "only" | "alone" | "tor-only" | "direct" => Mode::Only,
        _ => Mode::Chain,
    }
}

pub fn listen_address() -> SocketAddr {
    crate::settings::var("AETHER_TOR_BIND")
        .ok()
        .and_then(|value| value.trim().parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "127.0.0.1:1820".parse().expect("a literal address"))
}

pub fn http_listen_address() -> Option<SocketAddr> {
    crate::settings::var("AETHER_TOR_HTTP")
        .ok()
        .map(|value| value.trim().to_string())
        .filter(|value| !value.is_empty() && value != "off")
        .and_then(|value| value.parse().ok())
}

pub fn state_dir(base_config: &str) -> PathBuf {
    if let Some(dir) = crate::settings::var("AETHER_TOR_DIR")
        .ok()
        .filter(|d| !d.trim().is_empty())
    {
        return PathBuf::from(dir.trim());
    }

    let config = PathBuf::from(base_config);
    let stem = config
        .file_stem()
        .map(|name| name.to_string_lossy().to_string())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "aether".to_string());

    match config.parent() {
        Some(parent) if !parent.as_os_str().is_empty() => parent.join(format!("{stem}-tor")),
        _ => PathBuf::from(format!("{stem}-tor")),
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Bridges {
    Disabled,
    Manual(Vec<String>),
    Auto { forced: bool },
}

pub fn bridges_from_file() -> Vec<String> {
    let path = match crate::settings::var("AETHER_TOR_BRIDGE_FILE") {
        Ok(value) if !value.trim().is_empty() => value.trim().to_string(),
        _ => return Vec::new(),
    };

    let text = match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
        Ok(text) => text,
        Err(e) => {
            log::warn!("[-] cannot read the bridge file {path}: {e}");
            return Vec::new();
        }
    };

    let lines = read_bridge_lines(&text);
    if lines.is_empty() {
        log::warn!("[-] the bridge file {path} held no bridge line");
    } else {
        log::info!("[+] {} bridge(s) read from {path}", lines.len());
    }
    lines
}

pub fn read_bridge_lines(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    text.lines()
        .map(|line| line.trim())
        .filter(|line| !line.is_empty() && !line.starts_with('#'))
        .map(|line| {
            line.strip_prefix("Bridge ")
                .or_else(|| line.strip_prefix("bridge "))
                .unwrap_or(line)
                .trim()
                .to_string()
        })
        .filter(|line| !line.is_empty())
        .collect()
}

pub fn bridges() -> Bridges {
    let from_file = bridges_from_file();
    let raw = crate::settings::var("AETHER_TOR_BRIDGES").unwrap_or_default();
    let trimmed = raw.trim();

    if !from_file.is_empty() {
        let mut lines = from_file;
        if !matches!(
            trimmed.to_lowercase().as_str(),
            "" | "off"
                | "no"
                | "0"
                | "false"
                | "none"
                | "auto"
                | "on"
                | "1"
                | "yes"
                | "true"
                | "force"
        ) {
            lines.extend(read_bridge_lines(&trimmed.replace(';', "\n")));
        }
        return Bridges::Manual(lines);
    }

    match trimmed.to_lowercase().as_str() {
        "" => Bridges::Auto { forced: false },
        "off" | "no" | "0" | "false" | "none" => Bridges::Disabled,
        "auto" | "on" | "1" | "yes" | "true" | "force" => Bridges::Auto { forced: true },
        _ => {
            let lines: Vec<String> = trimmed
                .split(['\n', ';'])
                .map(|line| line.trim().to_string())
                .filter(|line| !line.is_empty())
                .collect();

            if lines.is_empty() {
                Bridges::Auto { forced: false }
            } else {
                Bridges::Manual(lines)
            }
        }
    }
}

pub fn bridge_lines() -> Vec<String> {
    match bridges() {
        Bridges::Manual(lines) => lines,
        _ => Vec::new(),
    }
}

pub fn transports() -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    crate::settings::var("AETHER_TOR_PT")
        .unwrap_or_default()
        .split(['\n', ';'])
        .filter_map(|entry| {
            let entry = entry.trim();
            if entry.is_empty() {
                return None;
            }
            match entry.split_once('=') {
                Some((protocol, path)) => {
                    Some((protocol.trim().to_string(), path.trim().to_string()))
                }
                None => Some(("obfs4".to_string(), entry.to_string())),
            }
        })
        .collect()
}

    fn init_tracing() {

            );

        let _ = tracing_subscriber::fmt()
            .with_env_filter(filter)
            .with_writer(std::io::stderr)
            .with_target(true)
            .try_init();
    }
    const REVERSE_ATTEMPTS: usize = 3;

    fn direct_probe() -> Duration {
        crate::settings::var("AETHER_TOR_DIRECT_SECS")
            .ok()
            .and_then(|value| value.trim().parse().ok())
            .map(Duration::from_secs)
            .unwrap_or(DIRECT_PROBE)
    }

    fn manual_transports() -> Vec<Transport> {
        let mut grouped: Vec<Transport> = Vec::new();

        for (protocol, path) in transports() {
            let path = PathBuf::from(path);
            match grouped.iter_mut().find(|held| held.path == path) {
                Some(held) if !held.protocols.contains(&protocol) => held.protocols.push(protocol),
                Some(_) => {}
                None => grouped.push(Transport {
                    protocols: vec![protocol],
                    path,
                }),
            }
        }

        grouped
    }

    fn announce(plan: &Plan) {
        let mut kinds: BTreeMap<String, usize> = BTreeMap::new();
        for line in &plan.lines {
            let kind = crate::bridges::transport_of(line).unwrap_or_else(|| "vanilla".to_string());
            *kinds.entry(kind).or_default() += 1;
        }

        if !plan.lines.is_empty() {
            let summary: Vec<String> = kinds
                .iter()
                .map(|(kind, count)| format!("{count} {kind}"))
                .collect();
            log::info!(
                "[+] tor has {} bridge(s) {}: {}",
                plan.lines.len(),
                plan.source,
                summary.join(", ")
            );
        }

        for transport in &plan.transports {
            log::info!(
                "[+] {} speaks {}",
                transport.path.display(),
                transport.protocols.join(", ")
            );
        }

        if !plan.missing.is_empty() {
            log::warn!(
                "[-] nothing here can speak {}; {}",
                plan.missing.join(", "),
                crate::bridges::install_hint()
            );
        }
    }

    async fn auto_plan(state: &Path, through: Option<SocketAddr>) -> Plan {
        let (lines, source) = crate::bridges::fetch(state, through).await;
        let lines = crate::bridges::keep_reachable(lines, through).await;
        let plan = crate::bridges::plan(lines, source, manual_transports());
        announce(&plan);
        plan
    }

    fn build_config(
        state: &Path,
        through: Option<SocketAddr>,
        plan: Option<&Plan>,
        slot: Option<&str>,
    ) -> Result<TorClientConfig> {
        prepare_dir(state)?;
        let home = match slot {
            Some(name) => state.join("attempts").join(name),
            None => state.to_path_buf(),
        };
        let cache = home.join("cache");
        let data = home.join("state");
        prepare_dir(&home)?;
        prepare_dir(&cache)?;
        prepare_dir(&data)?;

        let mut builder = TorClientConfigBuilder::default();
        builder
            .storage()
            .cache_dir(CfgPath::new(cache.to_string_lossy().to_string()));
        builder
            .storage()
            .state_dir(CfgPath::new(data.to_string_lossy().to_string()));

        // Without a tunnel to dial through, tor leaves through the upstream proxy, if there is one.
        let proxy = match through {
            Some(tunnel) => {
                Some(
                    format!("socks5://{tunnel}")
                        .parse()
                        .map_err(|e| TorError::Tunnel {
                            tunnel,
                            reason: format!("{e}"),
                        })?,
                )
            }
            None => upstream_proxy(),
        };
        if let Some(proxy) = proxy {
            builder.channel().outbound_proxy(proxy);
        } else if let Some(proxy) = crate::upstream::configured() {
            // Connecting directly would leave outside the proxy aether was told to dial through.
            return Err(TorError::UpstreamProxy(proxy.endpoint()).into());
        }

        if let Some(plan) = plan {
            let mut taken = 0usize;
            for line in &plan.lines {
                match line.parse::<BridgeConfigBuilder>() {
                    Ok(bridge) => {
                        builder.bridges().bridges().push(bridge);
                        taken += 1;
                    }
                    Err(e) => log::warn!("[-] skipping a bridge tor cannot read: {e}"),
                }
            }

            if taken == 0 {
                return Err(TorError::NoReadableBridges.into());
            }

            for transport in &plan.transports {
                let mut named = Vec::new();
                for protocol in &transport.protocols {
                    named.push(protocol.parse().map_err(|e| TorError::Transport {
                        protocol: protocol.to_string(),
                        reason: format!("{e}"),
                    })?);
                }

                let mut entry = arti_client::config::pt::TransportConfigBuilder::default();
                entry
                    .protocols(named)
                    .path(CfgPath::new(transport.path.to_string_lossy().to_string()))
                    .run_on_startup(true);
                builder.bridges().transports().push(entry);
            }
        }

        builder
            .build()
            .map_err(|e| TorError::Configuration(format!("{e}")).into())
    }

    struct AbortOnDrop(tokio::task::AbortHandle);

    impl Drop for AbortOnDrop {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            self.0.abort();
        }
    }

    struct Sleeper {
        client: Client,
        keep: bool,
    }

    impl Drop for Sleeper {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            if !self.keep {
                self.client.set_dormant(arti_client::DormantMode::Soft);
            }
        }
    }

    fn watch_progress(
        client: Client,
        label: &'static str,
        seen: std::sync::Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,
        started: std::time::Instant,
    ) -> AbortOnDrop {
        let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
            use futures::StreamExt;
            use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;

            let mut events = client.bootstrap_events();
            let mut shown = String::new();
            let mut best = 0u64;

            while let Some(status) = events.next().await {
                let reached = (status.as_frac().max(0.0) * 1000.0).round() as u64;
                if reached > best {
                    best = reached;
                    seen.store(started.elapsed().as_secs(), Ordering::Relaxed);
                }

                let line = status.to_string();
                if line == shown {
                    continue;
                }
                shown = line.clone();

                if status.blocked().is_some() {
                    log::warn!("[-] tor {label}: {line}");
                } else {
                    log::info!("[*] tor {label}: {line}");
                }
            }
        });

        AbortOnDrop(task.abort_handle())
    }

    async fn boot(
        config: TorClientConfig,
        label: &'static str,
        stall: Option<Duration>,
    ) -> Result<Client> {
        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};

        let client = TorClient::builder()
            .config(config)
            .create_unbootstrapped()
            .map_err(|e| TorError::Client(format!("{e}")))?;

        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
        let seen = std::sync::Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
        let _watcher = watch_progress(client.clone(), label, seen.clone(), started);
        let mut sleeper = Sleeper {
            client: client.clone(),
            keep: false,
        };

        let booted: Result<()> = match stall {
            None => client
                .bootstrap()
                .await
                .map_err(|e| AetherError::from(TorError::Bootstrap(format!("{e}")))),
            Some(limit) => {
                let handle = client.clone();
                let running = async move { handle.bootstrap().await };
                tokio::pin!(running);

                loop {
                    tokio::select! {
                        outcome = &mut running => {
                            break outcome
                                .map_err(|e| AetherError::from(TorError::Bootstrap(format!("{e}"))));
                        }
                        _ = tokio::time::sleep(STALL_CHECK) => {
                            let quiet = started
                                .elapsed()
                                .as_secs()
                                .saturating_sub(seen.load(Ordering::Relaxed));

                            if quiet >= limit.as_secs() {
                                break Err(TorError::NoHeadway(quiet).into());
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        };

        booted?;
        prove(&client, label).await?;

        sleeper.keep = true;
        Ok(client)
    }

    fn proof_target() -> (String, u16) {
        let raw = crate::settings::var("AETHER_TOR_CHECK").unwrap_or_default();
        let raw = raw.trim();

        if raw.is_empty() {
            return ("check.torproject.org".to_string(), 443);
        }

        match raw.rsplit_once(':') {
            Some((host, port)) => (host.to_string(), port.parse().unwrap_or(443)),
            None => (raw.to_string(), 443),
        }
    }

    async fn prove(client: &Client, label: &'static str) -> Result<()> {
        let (host, port) = proof_target();
        log::info!("[*] tor {label}: trying a way out through {host}:{port}");

        match tokio::time::timeout(PROOF_LIMIT, client.connect((host.as_str(), port))).await {
            Ok(Ok(_stream)) => {
                log::info!("[+] tor {label}: the way out is open");
                Ok(())
            }
            Ok(Err(e)) => Err(TorError::Unreachable {
                host,
                port,
                reason: format!("{e}"),
            }
            .into()),
            Err(_) => Err(TorError::Silent {
                host,
                port,
                seconds: PROOF_LIMIT.as_secs(),
            }
            .into()),
        }
    }

    struct Limits {
        attempts: usize,
        deadline: Option<Duration>,
        stall: Option<Duration>,
    }

    async fn stage(
        state: &Path,
        through: Option<SocketAddr>,
        plan: Option<&Plan>,
        label: &'static str,
        limits: Limits,
        slot: Option<&str>,
    ) -> Result<Client> {
        let Limits {
            attempts,
            deadline,
            stall,
        } = limits;
        let mut tried = 0usize;
        loop {
            tried += 1;
            let config = build_config(state, through, plan, slot)?;
            let run = boot(config, label, stall);

            let outcome = match deadline {
                Some(limit) => match tokio::time::timeout(limit, run).await {
                    Ok(result) => result,
                    Err(_) => Err(TorError::NoAnswer(limit.as_secs()).into()),
                },
                None => run.await,
            };

            match outcome {
                Ok(client) => return Ok(client),
                Err(e) if tried >= attempts => return Err(e),
                Err(e) => {
                    log::warn!("[-] tor {label} failed: {e}; trying again in {BOOTSTRAP_RETRY:?}");
                    tokio::time::sleep(BOOTSTRAP_RETRY).await;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    async fn establish(state: &Path, through: Option<SocketAddr>, rounds: usize) -> Result<Client> {
        let policy = bridges();

        if let Bridges::Manual(lines) = &policy {
            let plan = crate::bridges::plan(lines.clone(), "given by hand", manual_transports());
            announce(&plan);
            if plan.is_empty() {
                return Err(TorError::TransportMissing(crate::bridges::install_hint()).into());
            }
            return stage(
                state,
                through,
                Some(&plan),
                "over your bridges",
                Limits {
                    attempts: rounds,
                    deadline: None,
                    stall: None,
                },
                None,
            )
            .await;
        }

        let forced = matches!(policy, Bridges::Auto { forced: true });
        let may_fall_back = match (&policy, through) {
            (Bridges::Disabled, _) => false,
            (_, Some(_)) => forced,
            _ => true,
        };

        if !forced {
            let attempts = if may_fall_back { 1 } else { rounds };
            let deadline = may_fall_back.then(direct_probe);
            let tries = stage(
                state,
                through,
                None,
                "reaching the network",
                Limits {
                    attempts,
                    deadline,
                    stall: None,
                },
                Some("direct"),
            );
            match tries.await {
                Ok(client) => return Ok(client),
                Err(e) if !may_fall_back => return Err(e),
                Err(e) => log::warn!("[-] tor could not get through on its own: {e}"),
            }
        }

        if through.is_some() {
            log::warn!(
                "[-] a pluggable transport dials for itself, outside the tunnel; plain bridges go \
                 through it, so they are the ones that work on a network which blocks tor outright"
            );
        }

        let plan = auto_plan(state, through).await;
        if plan.is_empty() {
            return Err(TorError::BlockedWithoutTransport(crate::bridges::install_hint()).into());
        }

        if let Some(client) = try_each_transport(state, through, &plan).await? {
            return Ok(client);
        }

        stage(
            state,
            through,
            Some(&plan),
            "over bridges",
            Limits {
                attempts: rounds,
                deadline: None,
                stall: None,
            },
            Some("all"),
        )
        .await
    }

    fn bridge_probe() -> Duration {
        crate::settings::var("AETHER_TOR_BRIDGE_SECS")
            .ok()
            .and_then(|value| value.trim().parse().ok())
            .map(Duration::from_secs)
            .unwrap_or(BRIDGE_PROBE)
    }

    fn stall_limit() -> Duration {
        crate::settings::var("AETHER_TOR_STALL_SECS")
            .ok()
            .and_then(|value| value.trim().parse().ok())
            .map(Duration::from_secs)
            .unwrap_or(STALL_LIMIT)
    }

    async fn try_each_transport(
        state: &Path,
        through: Option<SocketAddr>,
        plan: &Plan,
    ) -> Result<Option<Client>> {
        let worked = crate::bridges::recall(state);
        let waves = crate::bridges::waves(plan, worked.as_deref());
        if waves.is_empty() {
            return Ok(None);
        }

        let deadline = bridge_probe();
        let names: Vec<&str> = waves.iter().map(|(name, _)| name.as_str()).collect();
        log::info!("[*] tor will try {} in turn", names.join(", then "));

        for (name, wave) in &waves {
            for round in 1..=WAVE_TRIES {
                let mut only = wave.clone();
                crate::bridges::shuffle(&mut only.lines);

                let where_to: Vec<String> = only
                    .lines
                    .iter()
                    .filter_map(|line| crate::bridges::address_of(line))
                    .map(|address| address.to_string())
                    .collect();

                log::info!(
                    "[*] {name}: go {round} of {WAVE_TRIES}, dropped after {}s without headway, \
                     over {}",
                    stall_limit().as_secs(),
                    if where_to.is_empty() {
                        format!("{} bridge(s)", only.lines.len())
                    } else {
                        where_to.join(", ")
                    }
                );

                let outcome = stage(
                    state,
                    through,
                    Some(&only),
                    "over bridges",
                    Limits {
                        attempts: 1,
                        deadline: Some(deadline),
                        stall: Some(stall_limit()),
                    },
                    Some(name.as_str()),
                )
                .await;

                match outcome {
                    Ok(client) => {
                        crate::bridges::remember(state, name);
                        log::info!("[+] {name} got through");
                        return Ok(Some(client));
                    }
                    Err(e) => log::warn!("[-] {name} did not get through: {e}"),
                }
            }
        }

        log::warn!("[-] no transport got through on its own; trying every bridge together");
        Ok(None)
    }

    fn announce_exit(proxy: SocketAddr, what: &'static str) {
        let proxy = crate::socks::dialable(proxy);
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            crate::exitloc::report_through_socks(proxy, what).await;
        });
    }

    /// Binds Tor's http proxy when one is asked for, with --tor-http.
    async fn bind_http() -> Result<Option<TcpListener>> {
        match http_listen_address() {
            Some(address) => Ok(Some(
                crate::socks::bind_listener("tor http proxy", address, "--tor-http").await?,
            )),
            None => Ok(None),
        }
    }

    async fn serve(
        listener: TcpListener,
        http: Option<TcpListener>,
        client: Client,
        kind: &'static str,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let connector = move |host: String, port: u16| {
            let client = client.clone();
            async move {
                client
                    .connect((host.as_str(), port))
                    .await
                    .map(|stream| {
                        use tokio_util::compat::FuturesAsyncReadCompatExt;
                        stream.compat()
                    })
                    .map_err(std::io::Error::other)
            }
        };

        // Served inside this future, so that it ends with it, letting go of its port, also when
        // the future is dropped as the core ends. Its failing leaves the socks5 one serving.
        let http_connector = connector.clone();
        let http_proxy = async move {
            if let Some(http_listener) = http {
                if let Err(e) = crate::socks::serve_http_connector(
                    http_listener,
                    "tor http proxy",
                    http_connector,
                )
                .await
                {
                    log::error!("[-] the tor http proxy stopped: {e}");
                }
            }
            std::future::pending::<std::convert::Infallible>().await
        };

        tokio::select! {
            outcome = crate::socks::serve_connector(listener, kind, connector) => outcome,
            never = http_proxy => match never {},
        }
    }

    /// The upstream proxy tor dials through when no tunnel carries it, see
    /// [crate::upstream::Upstream::tor_proxy]. One tor cannot read is one it cannot dial through,
    /// and is not printed, as it may carry a password.
    fn upstream_proxy() -> Option<ProxyProtocol> {
        crate::upstream::configured()?.tor_proxy()?.parse().ok()
    }

    /// Says how tor reaches the network when no tunnel carries it: through the upstream proxy, or
    /// directly when there is none; with one tor cannot dial through, tor does not start.
    fn announce_upstream() {
        let Some(proxy) = crate::upstream::configured() else {
            return;
        };
        match proxy.tor_proxy() {
            Some(_) => log::info!(
                "[*] tor dials out through the upstream proxy at {}",
                proxy.endpoint()
            ),
            None => log::warn!(
                "[-] tor cannot dial through the upstream proxy at {}, which is no socks5 address, \
                 or has a password and is not on this machine; it does not connect directly instead",
                proxy.endpoint()
            ),
        }
    }

    /// Waits for the core's socks5 server on `through`: the core holds its listener from its start
    /// and answers once a tunnel serves it.
    async fn wait_for_proxy(through: SocketAddr) {
        crate::socks::until_answered(through, Duration::from_secs(2), || {
            log::info!("[*] tor is waiting for the tunnel proxy at {through}")
        })
        .await
    }

    pub async fn run_chain(through: SocketAddr, state: PathBuf) -> Result<()> {
        init_tracing();
        let listen = listen_address();
        // Both held from the start, as the core holds its own: the user dials them while the
        // tunnel and Tor come up, and no other program may take them meanwhile.
        let listener = crate::socks::bind_listener("tor socks5", listen, "--tor-bind").await?;
        let listen = listener.local_addr().unwrap_or(listen);
        let http = bind_http().await?;

        wait_for_proxy(through).await;
        log::info!("[*] bootstrapping tor through the tunnel at {through}");

        let client = establish(&state, Some(through), FOREVER).await?;
        log::info!("[+] tor is ready; {listen} leaves through tor, carried by the tunnel");
        announce_exit(listen, "tor through the tunnel");

        serve(listener, http, client, "tor socks5").await
    }

    /// Tor with no tunnel underneath it, serving `listener`, which the core holds on `listen` from
    /// its start; its http proxy is held from the start as well.
    pub async fn run_only(listener: TcpListener, listen: SocketAddr, state: PathBuf) -> Result<()> {
        init_tracing();
        // The port the system gave, where --bind names port 0.
        let listen = listener.local_addr().unwrap_or(listen);
        let http = bind_http().await?;

        log::info!("[*] bootstrapping tor with no tunnel underneath it");
        announce_upstream();

        let client = establish(&state, None, FOREVER).await?;
        log::info!("[+] tor is ready; {listen} leaves through tor");
        announce_exit(listen, "tor");

        serve(listener, http, client, "tor socks5").await
    }

    /// Starts Tor for the tunnel to be dialled through: its socks5 address, and the handle that
    /// ends it with the core.
    pub async fn start_reverse(state: PathBuf) -> Result<(SocketAddr, crate::carrier::Carrier)> {
        init_tracing();
        let listen = listen_address();
        let listener = crate::socks::bind_listener("tor socks5", listen, "--tor-bind").await?;
        let http = bind_http().await?;
        // Where the tunnel dials Tor: where its listener is bound, a port 0 asked for being the port
        // the system picked.
        let dialled = crate::socks::dialable(listener.local_addr().unwrap_or(listen));

        log::info!("[*] bootstrapping tor; the tunnel will be dialled through it");
        // The upstream is still the proxy aether was given: the caller points it at tor once tor is up.
        announce_upstream();

        let client = establish(&state, None, REVERSE_ATTEMPTS).await?;
        log::info!("[+] tor is ready; the tunnel goes out through {dialled}");
        announce_exit(dialled, "tor");

        let serving =
            tokio::spawn(async move { serve(listener, http, client, "tor socks5").await });

        Ok((dialled, serving))
    }

    fn prepare_dir(path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(path)?;

        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
            let mut perms = std::fs::metadata(path)?.permissions();
            perms.set_mode(0o700);
            std::fs::set_permissions(path, perms)?;
        }

        Ok(())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn tor_errors_read_as_they_did_before_they_had_a_type() {
        let detail = |error: TorError| AetherError::from(error).detail();
        assert_eq!(detail(TorError::NoHeadway(30)), "no headway for 30s");
        assert_eq!(
            detail(TorError::Silent {
                host: "example.com".into(),
                port: 443,
                seconds: 45,
            }),
            "tor came up but example.com:443 stayed silent for 45s"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            detail(TorError::Tunnel {
                tunnel: "127.0.0.1:1819".parse().expect("an address"),
                reason: "refused".into(),
            }),
            "tor cannot dial through 127.0.0.1:1819: refused"
        );
        assert!(detail(TorError::NotBuiltIn).starts_with("this build has no tor support"));
    }

    /// The hold on the tor settings of a test: the variables are the whole process's, and the
    /// tests run side by side, so each test holds them first, or one clearing them would wipe a
    /// value another had just set. They start out clear, and are cleared again as the hold is
    /// let go, also by a test that failed half way.
    struct SettingsHeld {
        _held: std::sync::MutexGuard<'static, ()>,
    }

    impl Drop for SettingsHeld {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            clear();
        }
    }

    /// Waits for the hold on the tor settings, see `SettingsHeld`. A test that failed while it
    /// held them poisoned the lock, but cleared them all the same, so the lock is taken anyway.
    fn hold_settings() -> SettingsHeld {
        static SETTINGS: std::sync::OnceLock<std::sync::Mutex<()>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
        let held = SETTINGS
            .get_or_init(|| std::sync::Mutex::new(()))
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
        clear();
        SettingsHeld { _held: held }
    }

    fn clear() {
        crate::settings::remove("AETHER_TOR");
        crate::settings::remove("AETHER_TOR_DIR");
        crate::settings::remove("AETHER_TOR_BIND");
        crate::settings::remove("AETHER_TOR_BRIDGES");
        crate::settings::remove("AETHER_TOR_PT");
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_mode_has_a_spelling() {
        let _settings = hold_settings();
        assert_eq!(mode(), Mode::Off);
        for written in ["1", "on", "chain", "yes"] {
            crate::settings::set("AETHER_TOR", written);
            assert_eq!(mode(), Mode::Chain, "{written}");
        }
        for written in ["reverse", "rev", "warp-over-tor"] {
            crate::settings::set("AETHER_TOR", written);
            assert_eq!(mode(), Mode::Reverse, "{written}");
        }
        for written in ["only", "alone", "tor-only", "direct"] {
            crate::settings::set("AETHER_TOR", written);
            assert_eq!(mode(), Mode::Only, "{written}");
        }
        for written in ["0", "off", "false", "no"] {
            crate::settings::set("AETHER_TOR", written);
            assert_eq!(mode(), Mode::Off, "{written}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_state_dir_sits_beside_the_identity_file() {
        let _settings = hold_settings();
        assert_eq!(state_dir("aether.toml"), PathBuf::from("aether-tor"));
        assert_eq!(
            state_dir("/etc/aether/aether.toml"),
            PathBuf::from("/etc/aether/aether-tor")
        );
        crate::settings::set("AETHER_TOR_DIR", "/var/lib/aether-tor");
        assert_eq!(
            state_dir("aether.toml"),
            PathBuf::from("/var/lib/aether-tor")
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_tor_listener_has_a_default_of_its_own() {
        let _settings = hold_settings();
        assert_eq!(listen_address(), "127.0.0.1:1820".parse().unwrap());
        crate::settings::set("AETHER_TOR_BIND", "127.0.0.1:9150");
        assert_eq!(listen_address(), "127.0.0.1:9150".parse().unwrap());
    }

    #[test]
    fn bridges_are_read_one_per_entry() {
        let _settings = hold_settings();
        assert!(bridge_lines().is_empty());
        crate::settings::set(
            "AETHER_TOR_BRIDGES",
            "obfs4 192.0.2.55:38114 316E64 cert=abc iat-mode=0 ; obfs4 198.51.100.25:443 7DD627 cert=def",
        );
        let lines = bridge_lines();
        assert_eq!(lines.len(), 2);
        assert!(lines[0].starts_with("obfs4 192.0.2.55"));
        assert!(lines[1].starts_with("obfs4 198.51.100.25"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_transport_may_be_named_or_assumed_to_be_obfs4() {
        let _settings = hold_settings();
        assert!(transports().is_empty());
        crate::settings::set("AETHER_TOR_PT", "/usr/bin/lyrebird");
        assert_eq!(
            transports(),
            vec![("obfs4".to_string(), "/usr/bin/lyrebird".to_string())]
        );
        crate::settings::set(
            "AETHER_TOR_PT",
            "obfs4=/usr/bin/lyrebird;snowflake=/usr/bin/snowflake-client",
        );
        assert_eq!(
            transports(),
            vec![
                ("obfs4".to_string(), "/usr/bin/lyrebird".to_string()),
                (
                    "snowflake".to_string(),
                    "/usr/bin/snowflake-client".to_string()
                ),
            ]
        );
    }
}
